# dsh-retry
A retry executor plugin for DeepSeek Harness model requests: fixed-schedule retries, tuned for relay
endpoints and unstable upstreams.
## Quick start
[代码示例省略，未执行]
DeepSeek Harness retries failed model requests at the agent step boundary. The bundled executor (`@d
eepseek-ai/dsh-llm-retry`) takes its wait from a provider `retryPolicy` that only exposes exponentia
l backoff (`initialDelayMs`, `maxDelayMs`, `jitterRatio`). This plugin replaces that curve with an e
alDelayMs`, `maxDelayMs`, `jitterRatio`). This plugin replaces that curve with an explicit schedule:
| retry | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 and later |
| wait | 2s | 5s | 5s | 5s | 10s | 20s, unlimited |
A retried step is re-run inside the same open turn against the same durable history, so no partial a
nswer is duplicated and the model never sees the retry.
## Built for relay and pooled upstreams

A relay endpoint is a third-party API proxy that fans one key out across a pool
of upstream accounts

. It fails per account, not per request: a 401, an exhausted
quota or a 404 on one backend says noth

ing about the next attempt, and a public
gateway in front of the pool adds 5xx pages of its own. Thi

s executor is tuned
for that deployment and for unstable networks:

- **Per-account failures are retried.** `AUTH`, `QUOTA`, `ACCOUNT_QUOTA`,
`ACCOUNT_TOKEN_INVALID` an

d `INVALID_CREDENTIAL` are retried, and the
`HTTP_*` prefix covers every unclassified 4xx, so `HTTP_

404` is repeated
instead of ending the turn.
- **Gateway noise is retried.** Cloudflare and proxy 5x

x answers classify as
`SERVER`, including HTML error pages that never parse as JSON.
- **Corrupt str

eams are retried.** A broken SSE frame classifies as
`MALFORMED_RESPONSE`.
- **Waits stay short and

predictable.** 2s, 5s, 5s, 5s, 10s, then every 20s
without limit, so a short wobble costs seconds in

stead of an exponential climb
toward a ceiling.
- **No duplicated output.** Recovery re-runs the ste

p against the durable
history, so a retried request never repeats a half-finished answer.

The executor does not rotate accounts by itself: a retry only re-issues the
request, so the relay ha
s to select a different upstream for the next attempt.
## Why a separate executor

- Fixed delays: 2s, 5s, 5s, 5s, 10s, then a steady 20s tail instead of exponential growth.
- One unl

imited tail, for upstreams that eventually recover.
- Prefix matching for failure-code families, so

`HTTP_*` covers unclassified 4xx statuses such as `HTTP_404`.
- Standard `llm/retry` events, so the
Chat retry status row and the Trajectory panel keep working.
## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness `0.2.1-rc.5` (other releases may differ).
- Node.js `>=20.3`, which provides `Abo

ness `0.2.1-rc.5` (other releases may differ).
- Node.js `>=20.3`, which provides `AbortSignal.any`.
## Install

The package is a DSH bundle: `package.json` declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, so the
standard install als

o mounts the executor and retires the bundled one. No
hand-written patch is required.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Restart the profile afterwards; the composition is read at boot. The row then
appears under Plugins,
where its `config` is editable.

The shipped layer (cordis.patch.yml) inserts the executor
and disables `llm-retry`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Disabling `llm-retry` matters: two mounted executors would compete for the same
failure and both wri

te retry chain state. Keep the row disabled if the profile
overrides it.

## Configuration
| key | default | meaning |
| `schedule` | `[2000, 5000, 5000, 5000, 10000]` | wait in milliseconds before retries 1..n; the arr

ay length is the bounded head |
| `tailDelayMs` | `20000` | wait for every retry after the schedule

is exhausted |
| `retryableCodes` | see below | failure codes that are worth repeating |
A `retryableCodes` entry ending in `*` is a prefix rule. `HTTP_*` matches `HTTP_404`, `HTTP_409`, `H
TTP_422` and any other unclassified status. A bare `*` is rejected because it would match every fail
422` and any other unclassified status. A bare `*` is rejected because it would match every failure.
## Default retryable codes
| code | typical cause |

| `EMPTY_RESPONSE` | a completed response with no content blocks |
| `RATE_LIMIT` | HTTP 429 or a pr

ovider rate-limit error |
| `SERVER` | HTTP 5xx, including gateway and Cloudflare 5xx responses |
|

`TIMEOUT` | a request or stream deadline |
| `TRANSPORT` | connection reset, socket error, truncated

stream |
| `PI_AI_ERROR` | an upstream error the pi-ai adapter could not classify |
[该节后续省略]
## What you see
Each planned retry appends a durable `llm/retry` event, then `llm/retry-started` once the wait ends.
The Chat transcript renders a row such as `Retrying model request (2/5) . 4s` with an expandable fa
ilure reason and delay, and the Trajectory panel lists the attempt, error code and delay. Retries 6
and later render with an unlimited maximum.
No toast is raised, no partial output from a failed attempt is kept, and the model sees nothing: it
only receives the rebuilt request for the step that is being retried. Every attempt is a separately
billed provider request.
## Limitations
- The retry chain counter lives in memory per session. A host restart ends the turn, so nothing is l

ost that a durable counter would have preserved.
- Only agent-loop requests are retried. Direct `ctx

.llm.stream()` callers stay single-attempt.
- The tail is genuinely unlimited. When the upstream nev

er recovers, the turn stays in the retrying state until it is stopped.
- Retrying pooled credential
and quota failures assumes the pool rotates on the next attempt. A permanently exhausted pool loops
s assumes the pool rotates on the next attempt. A permanently exhausted pool loops every 20 seconds.
